title: Infra Playbook: GPU Fleet Capacity, Cloud Accounts & Networking, IaC Modules, CI/CD (2027)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our operational standards and runbooks for the GPU fleet, cloud account layout and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines and day-2 runbooks. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for capacity, reliability, and delivery of GPU-backed inference services (gpu-serve, fleet-manager, node-autoscaler).

Scope

- GPU fleet capacity planning and autoscaling policies
- Cloud account structure and cross-account networking patterns
- Terraform module conventions and module catalog guidance
- CI/CD build & promotion pipelines for infra modules and AMI/container builds
- Runbooks for common operational events (scale, upgrade, failover)

Owners and Contacts

- Primary owner: infra-platform (infra-platform@redwood.com)
- Oncall rotation: infra-sre oncall
- Module maintainers: see module catalog table below for per-module owners

Architecture Overview

We run GPU-backed inference pools across three account tiers: hosted-core (customer-facing inference), dedicated (reserved customer pools), and infra-shared (management, CI, observability). Networking is segmented by account; we use VPC peering + transit-gateway in AWS for latency-sensitive cross-account traffic, and explicit egress and NAT gating for telemetry. Key services:

- fleet-manager: scheduling, node allocation, and quota enforcement
- gpu-serve: per-service fronted inference daemonset (containerized)
- node-autoscaler: observes queued work and provisions nodes via cloud provider APIs and Terraform-managed autoscaling groups / instance fleets

GPU Fleet Capacity Planning

Goals and SLOs

- Allocation success: 99.9% of requests placed without provisioning delay > 150s (rolling 30d)
- Pool utilization target: 60-80% sustained across non-peak windows (avoid constant > 90%)
- Scale-up latency: 95th percentile node ready time <= 6 minutes (after instance launch)
- Cost efficiency: target nodes-per-GPU-utilization ratio to keep on-demand spend within forecast +/- 10%

Key Metrics to Track

- Node provisioning time (launch -> kube-ready)
- GPU utilization (per model-group and per-instance)
- Queue wait time and suffix backlog (requests/second queued > 0)
- Preemptible/spot eviction rate and replacement success
- Pod scheduling errors and OOMs

Scaling Policies (recommended defaults)

1. Buffer-based autoscaling: maintain a headroom buffer of N GPUs per pool. Default headroom: 8 GPUs for small pools (< 128 GPUs), 5% for larger pools.
2. Queue-time trigger: scale when 95th percentile queue time > 45s for 5 consecutive minutes.
3. Utilization trigger: scale-up when 95th percentile GPU utilization > 85% for 10 minutes; scale-down when 95th percentile utilization < 45% for 30 minutes.
4. Cooldown windows: 8 minutes after scale-up, 20 minutes after scale-down.
5. Preemptible usage: capped at 30% of pool by default; critical pools (SLA-backed) limited to 5%.

Capacity Playbook Steps (Short)

1. Evaluate current utilization and forecasted growth (see Capacity Dashboard).
2. Validate instance type compatibility (kernel/driver/AMIs) and required PCI-e topology.
3. Create a Terraform plan to add X instances to the pool (module: gpu-instance-fleet).
4. Roll out with canary nodes (10% of desired increase), monitor pod placement and scheduling logs.
5. Promote to full increase after 30m of stable metrics.

Cloud Accounts & Networking

Account Structure

- prod-hosted: customer workloads, PCI and encryption keys separated
- prod-dedicated: per-customer reserved pools (isolated sub-accounts)
- infra-shared: CI/CD runners, fleet-manager, shared observability (Prometheus, Loki)
- sandbox: development and experiments

Networking Patterns

- VPCs are per-account and per-region. Use Transit Gateway for high-throughput cross-account traffic; prefer VPC peering for single-region low-latency links.
- Subnet sizing: reserve /22 for GPU clusters to support node auto-scaling and pod CIDR allocations; ensure IPAM coordination with platform networking team.
- Security groups: minimal inbound rules, SSH restricted to bastion subnets. Egress controlled via proxy for telemetry.

Cross-account access

- Use IAM cross-account roles with short-lived STS credentials via our SSO service.
- Route traffic for inference control plane using private-links where supported; fall back to Transit Gateway with strict route tables.

Terraform / IaC Modules

Module Conventions

- Naming: module names are short and hyphenated (gpu-instance-fleet, vpc-transit, iam-service-roles).
- Inputs: require explicit owners, environment tag, and cost-center values. Avoid implicit defaults for region or instance-type.
- Outputs: export explicit IDs and ARNs (no nested maps).
- Versioning: semver for modules; pin module versions in root stacks (no floating >=).

Core Modules Catalog (examples)

- gpu-instance-fleet (owner: infra-platform) - manages ASG/instance-fleet, launch templates, and GPU driver bootstrap
- vpc-transit (owner: infra-network) - creates transit-gateway attachments and shared route tables
- iam-service-roles (owner: infra-security) - standardized roles for fleet-manager, node-autoscaler, CI runners
- ami-builder (owner: infra-ci) - Packer pipeline + SSM parameters for AMI distribution

Example usage snippet (Terraform-style, included as plaintext in this doc):

```
module "gpu_fleet_prod" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.redwood.com/infra/modules//gpu-instance-fleet?ref=v1.3.0"
  name   = "prod-hosted-gpu-fleet"
  owners = ["infra-platform@redwood.com"]
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge", "p4de.24xlarge"]
  target_gpu_count = 256
  spot_percentage = 20
}
```

CI/CD and Build Pipelines

Pipeline Patterns

- Mono-repo for modules: changes to modules trigger module unit tests and plan previews.
- Promote by tag: PR -> merge to main triggers plan and applies to sandbox; manual promotion (tag vX.Y.Z) triggers apply to prod via gated workflow.
- AMI/container builds are published with immutable tags and promoted via image-repository promotion steps.

Pipeline Requirements

- All terraform applies to prod require: 2 approvers, successful terratest, and a preflight canary apply to a sandbox account.
- Secrets and credentials must be provided by the secrets-manager pipeline (not hard-coded).
- Pipelines must record change-sets and link to ticket/owner in the commit message.

Runbooks (Operational Procedures)

Scale Up (manual emergency)

1. Notify infra-sre channel and raise a support incident.
2. Validate drivers and AMI compatibility using AMI health check script (link to ami-builder).
3. Create a Terraform change in the sandbox: increase target_gpu_count by X. Run plan and validate.
4. Apply to prod using gated pipeline with 2 approvers.
5. Monitor node readiness, pod scheduling, and queue time. Revert if pod placement errors exceed 1% in the first 15 minutes.

Scale Down (cost optimization)

1. Confirm utilization trend < 45% over 72 hours and no queued backlog.
2. Schedule a scale-down with customer-ops if any dedicated pools affected.
3. Apply Terraform change with staggered 10% decrements and observe metrics for 24 hours between steps.

GPU Driver or Kernel Update

1. Build AMI in sandbox via ami-builder.
2. Bake canary cluster (1-2 nodes) and run regression prompts and perf tests.
3. If stable for 24 hours, roll canary to 10% of pool, then 50%, then full. Use automated rollback on scheduling failures > 2% or provisioning errors.

Incident: Node Eviction Flood (spot reclaim)

1. Verify eviction rates and determine if spot market is safe.
2. If eviction rate > 5% and replacement < target within 15 minutes, increase on-demand capacity via terraform and reduce spot_percentage.
3. Notify cost team and file postmortem if customer impact occurred.

Day-2 Operations and Playbook Maintenance

- Quarterly capacity review: infra-platform + SRE + product to update forecast and instance types.
- Module hygiene: maintain semantic versioning, deprecate modules with migration guides.
- Postmortems: use incident-review template and link to PRs/changes that contributed to incident.

Checklist Before Significant Infra Changes

- Run terratest suite and validate plan output for resource counts.
- Smoke test on sandbox environment with synthetic workload (1000 requests over 10m).
- Notify stakeholders and scheduled maintenance windows for potential customer impact.
- Ensure runbook and rollback steps are documented in the PR description.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Links

- Terraform plan for prod GPU fleet: `make tf-plan TARGET=prod-hosted-gpu-fleet`
- AMI health check: `scripts/ami-health-check.sh --ami-id <AMI>`
- Capacity dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/infra/gpu-capacity-overview
- CI/CD pipelines: https://ci.redwood.com/pipelines/infra
